external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers who upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal
external_entities.notes: The source refers to this entity in the plural as “Suppliers”.

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers who review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
external_entities.notes: The source refers to this entity in the plural as “category managers”.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The SaaS vendor that hosts the portal and pushes supplier data extracts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: Service that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where uploaded compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: Bucket in the organisation's cloud account receiving the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: Database into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Supplier signs in to the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: Supplier uploads compliance paperwork through the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff

data_flows.name: store paperwork
data_flows.description: The portal stores uploaded compliance documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_flows.name: review and approve
data_flows.description: Category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it through the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: uploaded compliance paperwork and approval or rejection

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: The vendor platform pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The source says, “We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end.” The runbook separately says, “the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.” These are conflicting claims about encryption in transit, so the value is unknown.

data_flows.name: load file
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the supplier data extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes the extracted records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting environment for the SaaS portal and vendor platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier document portal presents a web interface because the source calls it a portal.
assumptions.basis: The source names the component “Supplier document portal”; the extraction convention treats a portal as a web interface.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor hosting environment is a tenant boundary because the vendor, a different party, hosts the SaaS product and the organisation does not run it.
assumptions.basis: “The portal is a SaaS product. The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.”

assumptions.assumption: The organisation's cloud account is a network boundary distinct from the corporate network because the listed components run in the cloud account rather than the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source places the bucket, service, and database in “our cloud account” and separately places category managers on the “corporate network”.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform's data is confidential because it holds compliance paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source says the platform holds insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket's data is confidential because it holds the supplier data extract derived from supplier paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source says the bucket receives a supplier data extract, and the described supplier data includes staff contact details and compliance paperwork.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database's data is confidential because it holds supplier records derived from supplier paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source says the database receives supplier records from the extract, whose described contents include staff contact details and compliance paperwork.
